title: Shared band table: centres, weights, faint thresholds, kernels and readability windows
description: One table for every consumer of band readings (organic-evidence levels, ZooMS pattern, C1, close-ups). A reading r_b = mean of E over centre +- half_width_nm, E = scale x Savitzky-Golay derivative of absorbance (kernel 'e31'). u_b = r_b / weight. Band readability is ONE gate per band, shared by the evidence levels and the ZooMS pattern (so a close-up always matches the call): readable unless SD_E > 0.25 x weight and r_b < 1.5 x weight (thresholds owned by the rule files). SD_E = gain x envelope_factor x N2(readability noise window) on the AS-MEASURED scan; the engine computes the gain (format 2) from the band's plain kernel (a projection is ignored), the correction actually applied to the stream (its blur and absorbance gain per detector segment, linearised) and the scan's own detector joins, under noise_model. When the gain cannot be computed (a non-linear correction; a kernel or noise window not inside one detector segment of the scan: not available on this instrument) or N2 is not finite, SD_E is +infinity: the band is unreadable unless strong, and the result says the band noise is unknown. A band with a 'projection' is read on that projection's corrected E (see 'projections'); u_b = u_sign x r_b / weight (u_sign -1: a trough, more collagen = more negative E; default +1).

consumers: plaster, wax, ester and heat signs (their own parameter files)

n2.definition: canonical N2 (reference/spyder_ref/n2.py): A = log10(1/max(R, 1e-4)) on the full as-measured grid; second difference centred on each channel; centres lo <= lambda < hi; 1.4826 x MAD; units 1e-5
n2.measured_on: the AS-MEASURED scan, never the transferred stream

noise_model.description: white noise in absorbance smoothed by a Gaussian of this sigma (nm), independent between detector segments (the ASD files' own residual autocorrelation); taps to +-8 sigma. A correction file may give its instrument's own value in provenance.instrument_noise.correlation_nm, measured on that instrument's scans (another instrument, or a resampled grid, has its own).

oh1500.description: x = E / kernel scale over window_nm (the SG31 cubic second derivative of absorbance, model units); x' = x - v (v . (x - c)); E' = kernel scale x x'. A band naming this projection is read as the mean of E' over centre +- half_width_nm.

source.direction: the altered OH / bound-water direction of the OH-corrected 1500 nm model (recovered from public data; unit length)

readability.envelope_provenance: phase 0c h05/h14: within-detector noise envelope (Monte Carlo with the real high-resolution wavelength envelope / the shipped gain; nearly identical for every transfer key); same-bone scatter of a high-resolution variation set consistent (C-H 1.8-2.4x the uncorrected prediction, an upper bound). A default for any correction; an instrument may carry its own factors in the correction file's provenance.instrument_noise.ch_envelope_factors (the median 4th-difference noise ratio over at least 10 of its scans), never one per scan.
readability.note: SD_E = gain x envelope_factor x N2(noise_window_nm) on the AS-MEASURED scan; the gain is computed for the correction applied to the stream the band is read on and the scan's own detector segments (format 2; format 1 listed it per transfer file).

readability.window_choice: Phase 0b item 17: 2220-2245 nm (band-free, between the 2206 clay and 2254 ester regions, nearer 2262/2284 than 2000-2100). Every candidate (2000-2100, 2100-2150, 2215-2245, 2220-2245, 2225-2250, each with and without a noise-shape factor) gave identical ZooMS verdicts on the 36 high-res scans of concordant pairs (agreement with the standard-res partner 30/36 for all; kappa undefined-low because every partner reads Good), identical can't-tell rates on the noisy high-res session (22.5%) and the variation set (19.3%), and identical results under 2-4x added noise; the tie goes to the band-free window nearest the bands (its noise is 1.26-1.36x lower than at 2262/2284, against 1.5-1.67x for 2000-2100). Zero verdict or evidence-level changes on any cohort.

readability.gain_source: the band's plain kernel (the projection is ignored: the simulated SD of the projected reading is about 10% below it, so the gate errs on the cautious side)

provenance.weights_and_faint: weights = median band ratios over the reference bones with >= 1% yield (public calibration data); faint thresholds = rounded 99th percentiles of collagen-free archaeological fauna (statistics only, unreleased collection, anonymised)
provenance.gains: computed by the engine (format 2; DECISIONS 137): detector-local correlated noise (white noise in absorbance smoothed by a 1.25 nm Gaussian) propagated exactly through the band kernel and the correction (each detector segment's blur matrix transposed, times its absorbance gain), linearised; Monte Carlo through the engine agrees to 0.2% (and tracks composed files and other joins within 0.3%). The format-1 gains recorded for no transfer, v0.1 and v0.2 are reproduced within their 6-decimal rounding (max relative 8.5e-5).
provenance.gate_reconciliation: Phase 0b item 11. The gate's gains are the correlated-noise gains (0.017729 E per N2 standard; 0.008441 after v0.1), not white-noise values. The ~2x excess found by an earlier Monte Carlo is real non-stationary noise: on noisy high-res scans, N2 near 1689/1728 is 1.6-2.2x N2(1500-1600) and near 2262/2284 1.5-2.2x N2(2000-2100) (detector response falls toward the detector ends; a curvature-free high-pass estimate agrees). Scaling the SWIR1 C-H gates by that shape (x1.64 / x1.76) made the high-res evidence level agree LESS with the standard-res partner (kappa 0.78 -> 0.55; 2.5% more can't tell on the noisy session), so the gate keeps window N2 with the analytic gains: SD_E is a calibrated noise index, about half the true local SD at the far C-H bands on noisy high-res scans. Gains refreshed for transfer v0.2 (SWIR1 x 0.7050/0.6343, SWIR2 x 0.6258/0.6343).
